findings.title: Dead end: talk_never_won

findings.detail: average/11: 81 of 124 completed missions were re-runs of a faded fix; the campaign took 509 days (campaign_done) against the expert's 177
findings.fix: A reopened main mission takes the only main slot for another 14+ days, so new missions wait. Let a reopened mission come back as a side mission (or a short 're-standardise' task without a new Check), and make decay_days longer than the Check so one lapse is not a full redo.
findings.title: Treadmill: players who do not always standardise spend most of the campaign redoing faded fixes

findings.detail: careless ends at € -50.000 after 1098 days, still falling about € 148 a month; 2 bad periods
findings.fix: CLAUDE.md: recovery must always be possible. Open problems (and worn fixes) keep costing and the bad period cuts capacity, while rewards come only from solved problems. Add a floor (e.g. the board grants a recovery budget, or costs stop at a debt limit), or let a bad period lower costs (no overtime) instead of only capacity.
findings.title: Debt spiral: the budget keeps falling and the bad period never ends

findings.detail: cm standard_designs, predicted throughput +8.7 % (fix), problem KPI throughput +8.7 % (fix), -32.3 % (before/after), capacity +26.2 % (fix), eff 0.90, lesson cause_right
findings.fix: The verdict now uses the Check's counterfactual (Region.check's forecast: the coming lead time with and without the fix), but CheckPanel still shows before/after, two different 14-day windows, so the stream's own trend lands on the player's fix. Show forecast.without ('zonder jouw maatregel') and forecast.with as the columns, and say how far ahead the Check looks (forecast.days).
findings.title: The Check panel's before/after table shows the problem's KPI worse although the fix helped

findings.detail: cm planning_with_fault_windows, predicted first_time_right +10.7 % (fix), problem KPI first_time_right +10.7 % (fix), -5.1 % (before/after), capacity +0.0 % (fix), eff 0.42, lesson too_early
findings.fix: A too-early countermeasure weakens the problem, but below Pdca.CHECK_PASS it does not work: the verdict and the numbers disagree. Word the too_early lesson with the numbers ('het helpt een beetje, maar werkt maar half').
findings.title: Check fails while the fix moved the predicted KPI

findings.fix: See the slowest missions; shorten Checks or let the player run missions in parallel.
findings.title: Campaign not finished within the horizon

findings.fix: After two mismatches the coach (or the Check panel) should point at the clues that rule the countermeasure out; today the only feedback is the mismatch note.
findings.title: A player can fail the Check 8 times in a row without a way out

findings.detail: cm delegated_approval, predicted capacity +14.7 % (fix), problem KPI throughput +7.5 % (fix), +0.0 % (before/after), capacity +14.7 % (fix), eff 0.55, lesson cause_wrong
findings.fix: By design the fit decides the pass and the lesson says cause_wrong, so a lucky countermeasure passes. Lower eff when the cause is wrong (e.g. x0.6), or make the root-cause dimension of the score cost more.
findings.title: A wrong root cause still passes the Check

findings.detail: cm readiness_check, predicted lead_time +8.6 % (fix), problem KPI lead_time +8.6 % (fix), -5.1 % (before/after), capacity +0.0 % (fix), eff 0.90, lesson cause_right
findings.fix: Check that the countermeasure's effects touch the constraint's touch time or availability; otherwise the 'bottleneck first' lesson reads false.
findings.title: A fix at the constraint passes but stream capacity does not rise

findings.detail: 102 distinct lines over 153 expert asks; 6 lines reach 5+ missions, e.g. "En hoe is het nu echt, op de werkvloer? Wat zie je daar?" in 11 missions. Insights: 43 of 153 asks.
